problem: Reversing the weights before calling reference_impl.allocate and reversing the result after flips the documented lowest-index tie-break to highest-index, so allocate('0.01',[1,1]) returns [0.00, 0.01] instead of main's [0.01, 0.00] (and the first invalid weight reported changes too).

The production module now imports reference_impl, a test-oracle-named module resolved via sys.path, so which implementation runs depends on the environment and any oracle comparison becomes tautological.

list(weights) now runs before places and amount are validated, changing the raised exception (e.g. allocate('1', None, places=-1) raises TypeError instead of ValueError) and consuming generator weights even when the call then fails on places or amount.
The Fraction and Decimal imports are unused on the branch (ruff F401).
_to_decimal is dead code that duplicates reference_impl._to_decimal, which is the copy that actually runs.
The whole implementation is replaced without any test, and a single tie-break test would have caught F1.
